aliases: 35th Street and Martin Luther King Jr. Drive
description: Monument at 35th St and Martin Luther King Jr. Dr constructed in 1927 honoring the Eighth Regiment's World War I service; doughboy sculpture added 1936.

name: Rhumboogie Café
description: Nightclub at 343 E. 55th St opened April 1942; destroyed by fire December 31, 1945; reopened June 1946; closed May 1947.

name: Johnson Publishing Company Building
description: Building at 820 S. Michigan Ave; Johnson Publishing Company moved here in December 1971; home of Ebony and Jet magazines.

name: East 63rd Street Corridor
description: East 63rd Street, documented as a Black nightlife and entertainment corridor extending into Woodlawn; no fixed numerical boundaries asserted.

description: Site of the original Comiskey Park (1910–1990), where Disco Demolition Night was held on July 12, 1979; ballpark demolished 1991.

sources.citation: Chicago History Museum: Disco Demolition Night

description: Living memorial in Marquette Park dedicated August 5, 2016, marking the 50th anniversary of Dr. King's August 5, 1966 open-housing march.

name: Record Row
description: South Michigan Avenue corridor once lined with Black-owned record labels, distributors, and studios

notes: Nickname and exact extent vary across sources; corridor concept is well attested.

name: Great Migration
description: Movement of about six million African Americans from the rural South to the urban North, Midwest, and West, reshaping Chicago's Black Belt.

description: Racial violence from July 27 to August 3, 1919, ignited by the killing of Eugene Williams at the segregated 29th Street beach.

description: Robert Sengstacke Abbott publishes the first issue of the Chicago Defender in May 1905 (sources differ on May 5 vs. May 6).

name: Savoy Ballroom Opening
description: The Savoy Ballroom opens at 4733 S. Parkway on November 23, 1927.

name: Regal Theater Opening
description: The Regal Theater opens at 4719 S. Parkway on February 4, 1928.

name: First Bud Billiken Parade
description: First Bud Billiken Parade held August 11, 1929; founded by Chicago Defender publisher Robert S. Abbott as a celebration of Black youth and education.

description: First national Negro History Week launched in February 1926 by Carter G. Woodson through the Association for the Study of Negro Life and History; precursor to Black History Month.

name: Rhumboogie Café Opening
description: The Rhumboogie Café nightclub opens at 343 E. 55th St in April 1942.

name: Rhumboogie Café Reopening
description: The Rhumboogie Café reopens in June 1946 after the 1945 fire.

name: Rhumboogie Café Closure
description: The Rhumboogie Café closes permanently in May 1947.

name: Chess Records Founded
description: The Chess brothers acquire Aristocrat Records and rename it Chess Records in 1950.

description: Vee-Jay Records established in Gary, Indiana, in 1953; later operated from Chicago offices including 1449 S. Michigan Ave.

description: The Club DeLisa nightclub closes on February 16, 1958.

name: Regal Theater Demolition
description: The Regal Theater, closed since 1968, is demolished in 1973.

description: Anti-disco promotion between games of a White Sox doubleheader at the original Comiskey Park on July 12, 1979, ends in a riot and field destruction.

name: Harold Washington Elected Mayor
description: Harold Washington is elected on April 12, 1983, becoming Chicago's first Black mayor.

description: Mass gathering of Black men in Washington, D.C., on October 16, 1995, called by Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan; mobilization anchored in Chicago.

description: Fire guts the historic Pilgrim Baptist Church at 3301 S. Indiana Ave on January 6, 2006, during roof restoration work.

aliases: Martin Luther King Jr. Living Memorial dedication

description: Glossy monthly magazine founded by John H. Johnson celebrating Black achievement, culture, and photojournalism.

description: Magazine founded by John H. Johnson; renamed Black World in 1970, it became a leading Black Arts Movement journal under Hoyt W. Fuller.

description: Official newspaper of the Nation of Islam (1960–1975); at its peak the most widely read Black-operated newspaper in the U.S.

description: Twice-monthly official newspaper of the Nation of Islam, published from Chicago.
